items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I’ve had Nat Cole record a few tunes and Count Basie and Woody Herman and Cannonball Adderley and George Shearing just recently recorded.

ctx.x: And that allowed you to do some arranging later on?

Well I learned, well I did a lot of writing of songs, a lot of writing of compositions, a lot. I’ve written about three hundred, and about 280 of them have been recorded, but mostly by myself, but I’ve had Nat Cole record a few tunes and Count Basie and Woody Herman and Cannonball Adderley and George Shearing just recently recorded. I don’t push my songs. I feel strange pushing songs on people. But sometimes they hear them and I get a call, did you write this? Recently, in the last few years, Nat Cole recorded…

recorded both of them. Now not much records sold in those days, but that was 1948. Now — and he died and they weren’t pushing his records. Now Natalie Cole comes out with that “Unforgettable” with her dad, and piecing that thing together. So that made Nat a little hot too, they started re-releasing his records. And “Peaches” came out again. And that brought me a little money. And then George Shearing, about a year and a half ago did an album called “A Tribute to Nat Cole” and recorded that song. Someone told me…
